subject: Reserved capacity proposal — GPU cost sensitivity & approval path for ACME AI
messages:
From: Julia Smith <j.smith@acmeai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity inquiry + pricing sensitivity

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked great. ACME is evaluating a committed reserved capacity purchase to support a new inference pipeline (beta launch Q4). Two asks to move the procurement conversation forward:

1) Can you share sizing scenarios (12/24/36-month commits) tied to GPU SKU mixes and what the unit price sensitivity is if GPU hardware costs move +/- 20%?
2) What internal approval thresholds or discount tiers would apply if we need ~300 reserved slots at peak — and how quickly can you turn up Dedicated pools in us-west?

If you can send a one-page scenario matrix and any proposed contract language for hedging vs pass-through, procurement would like that for their next meeting (Thu).

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 30m call if helpful.

— Julia
Procurement, ACME AI

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Smith <j.smith@acmeai.com>
Cc: Tom Zhao <tom.zhao@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity inquiry + pricing sensitivity

Hi Julia — thanks, excited to work this through. Attached is an initial spreadsheet (commit_scenarios.xlsx) with three term/sku mixes, modeled utilization assumptions, and a sensitivity column that adjusts Redwood's unit price by +/- 20% to reflect GPU cost swings. Key points up-front:

- Base ask modeled: 300 reserved slots (mixture of h100-equivalent and a100-equivalent serving pools)
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 150ms for 75-token responses; we modeled tails at burst = 1.5x baseline
- Economics: 24-month looks to be the best trade-off for ACME given forecasted load volatility; 36-month gives deeper discounts but requires stronger commit certainty

I also flagged a potential approval ask: any discount beyond 30% off list will need VP sign-off (per our standard pricing matrix). I can route for approvals if you confirm preferred term and target discount band.

Would you like a short call Wed morning to run through the numbers?

Thanks,
Monica
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding ACME's ask and the attached scenarios (commit_scenarios.xlsx). Short summary of where we are and what I need: 

- Customer: ACME AI — asking for 300 reserved slots, wants sensitivity to GPU cost swings (+/-20%) and approval thresholds for discounts.
- Preferred term from customer: leaning 24 months, open to 36 for bigger discount.
- Our modeling shows three SKU mixes; the aggressive discount requires us to assume 70% utilization sustained.

Can each of you weigh in on: 
  - Karthik: approve discount bands and the approval path (what % needs VP/CFO signoff?)
  - Laura: confirm finance comfort with revenue recognition and any capex pass-through language we should avoid/require
  - Marcus: feasibility for Dedicated pools in us-west for a 300-slot commit and expected lead time to guarantee the SKUs 

I've included internal notes in the attachment internal_commit_notes.txt (short bullets & risk table). If we can get internal alignment by EOD tomorrow, I can send a firm proposal back to ACME Thu morning.

Thanks — Monica

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity inquiry + pricing sensitivity — need pricing/ops guidance

Monica — quick notes from pricing/finance ops: 

- Discount tiers we can authorize (guided):
  * up to 15%: AM/AE sign-off only
  * 15–30%: Sales Director + Revenue Ops approval
  * 30–40%: VP Sales sign-off required (inform Finance)
  * >40%: Requires CFO/Head of Revenue approval and legal to review concession language

- For a 24-month 300-slot commit, base case discount we can consider is 28–32% depending on upfront payment cadence and minimum utilization guarantee. If the customer accepts a utilization floor (e.g., 55% monthly), we can grant the deeper end of that band.

- Hedging options: suggest adding a GPU-cost-pass-through clause with a quarterly reconciliation mechanism tied to an agreed index (we typically use an internal compute-cost index but can map to public GPU spot price proxies). If ACME wants a fixed unit price regardless of market, we should widen the margin and require stronger commit language.

- Approval timing: VP sign-off can be obtained within 48 hours if we have an exec summary and revenue impact table. CFO elevation adds ~5 business days.

I'll prepare a pricing_approval_matrix.pdf and a short approval memo if you want to route.

-Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity inquiry + pricing sensitivity — infra availability

Folks — operational feasibility notes: 

- Capacity: We can provision a 300-slot Dedicated pool in us-west but SKU mix matters. Recommended approach: target a 3:1 split H100-equivalent : A100-equivalent for low-latency workloads, with an escape hatch to convert 10% to cheaper SKUs for batch reranking workloads.
- Lead time: If we can accept existing cloud partners' spare capacity, we can stand up the pool in ~14 days. If we need procurement of specific GPUs, plan for 6–8 weeks.
- Overcommit buffer: Recommend a 15% buffer on top of peak to avoid tail latencies during ramp; include an auto-burst clause into on-demand pools for bursts > 110% of committed QPS.
- Risk: If GPU market costs spike >20%, our margin on deep discounts compresses quickly. The pass-through clause Karthik suggested mitigates that but will be resisted by procurement usually.

Happy to provide a runbook and expected SLA credit schedule for different term/commit combos.
— Marcus
Director, Infrastructure Planning

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity inquiry + pricing sensitivity — finance review

Team — flagged items from finance perspective: 

1) Revenue recognition: For 24/36-month prepaid deals we need clear billing milestones. If ACME requests monthly billing, we'll amortize revenue but need a purchase order and minimum monthly utilization clause to avoid churn risk.
2) Discount governance: Agree with Karthik — require VP sign-off for >30%. Any concession that includes a pass-through mechanism must have a floor protection for Redwood (i.e., we cannot price below X USD/hr equivalent).
3) Contractual terms to include: SLA credits schedule, early termination fee (declining over time), and a contingency for hardware cost pass-through reconciliations.

I've attached the pricing_approval_matrix.pdf with recommended sign-off names and thresholds. If we need CFO sign-off, route through me and I will prepare the executive memo.

- Laura
Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Smith <j.smith@acmeai.com>, Tom Zhao <tom.zhao@acmeai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-04T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed reserved capacity offer & next steps (ACME)

Hi Julia / Tom — thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Attached is a proposed commit table (proposed_commit_term_table.csv) and the approval matrix. High-level proposal: 

- Offer A (24 months): 300 slots, 70% H100-equivalent / 30% A100-equivalent, 28% discount off list, monthly billing with 55% minimum utilization guarantee OR a 10% higher discount if prepaid annually.
- Offer B (36 months): 300 slots, same SKU split, 35% discount off list, prepaid up-front or annual prepay required. This includes a quarterly GPU-cost reconciliation clause: +/- 10% of GPU index — no adjustment; beyond +/- 10% we carve a 50/50 pass-through adjustment unless customer elects a fixed-price rider (higher discount required).
- Operational: We can provision Dedicated pools in us-west in ~14 days against existing partner capacity; 6–8 weeks if specific procurement required. We recommend a 15% buffer and an auto-burst to on-demand to handle peak spikes.

Next steps:
1) Let us know preferred offer (A vs B) and whether ACME agrees to the 55% utilization floor or annual prepay.
2) If you pick Offer B and accept the pass-through reconciliation, we'll route for VP sign-off (estimated 48 hours). If >35% discount is requested beyond the table, we'll need CFO review (~5 business days).
3) If accepted, I'll send a DocuSign link for a statement of work + reserved capacity addendum.

Attaching the commit table and the approval matrix. Happy to jump on a 30m call tomorrow to walk through.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Julia — quick follow-up with the two items: 

1) SLA-credit schedule (example):
   - p95 latency breach > 2 consecutive days: 5% credit of monthly fee
   - p95 latency breach > 5 consecutive days: 15% credit of monthly fee + tech escalation
   - sustained availability < 99.5% in a billing month: pro-rated credit up to 25%

2) Pass-through index & reconciliation (example):
   - Index: quarterly average of GPU spot-equivalent index published by public cloud provider + internal oss adjustment (we will share the calculation table in the SOW).
   - Example: If index increases 18% in quarter, first 10% absorbed by Redwood; remaining 8% — 50/50 split -> ACME pays 4% additional on that quarter's committed compute charges. Detailed formula in SOW.

I'll attach a one-page example calculation and the SLA credit runbook to the SOW when I send the DocuSign link.

Thanks — Monica
